node.title: Re: Arrays and Handles Problem (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
To give a little more information in addition to [holli]'s [id://1233276|answer]: foreach (@testarray) loops over the array and assigns each element to [doc://$_], plus that iterator variable $_ is an alias to each original element of the array (see [doc://perlsyn#Foreach-Loops]), meaning that assigning to $_ changes the value in the original array. while () is actually while (defined($_ = readline DATA)) ([doc://perlop#I/O-Operators]), i.e. it is assigning to the same [doc://$_] variable.

If you use an explicit loop variable in the foreach, e.g. foreach my $elem (@testarray), the problem goes away, and you can also do the same in the while, e.g. while ( my $line = ).

Update: Here you can see @testarray getting clobbered. The undef comes from the fact that returns undef when it hits EOF (end of file).

use warnings; use strict; use Data::Dump; my @testarray = ([10,20],[30,40]); dd "A", @testarray; foreach (@testarray) { dd "B", @testarray; while ( ) { dd "C", @testarray; } dd "D", @testarray; } dd "E", @testarray; __DATA__ hello world

Output:

("A", [10, 20], [30, 40]) ("B", [10, 20], [30, 40]) ("C", "hello\n", [30, 40]) ("C", "world\n", [30, 40]) ("D", undef, [30, 40]) ("B", undef, [30, 40]) ("D", undef, undef) ("E", undef, undef)
